summary: Learn digital trust, identity and customer authentication with NIST SP 800-63, practical workshops, and board-ready outputs.
lede: Customer identity controls connect identity proofing, authentication and recovery to help assess access risk consistently. For IAM, fraud, cybersecurity, onboarding and identity-governance professionals, the course addresses how to design and govern customer access controls. Exercises build skills in evaluating proofing evidence, selecting assurance levels, designing authentication and recovery flows, mapping identity lifecycles, and creating federation assessments, privacy controls and governance scorecards.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who own, influence, or govern digital trust and identity and customer authentication controls across customer-facing systems.
prerequisites: Participants should have an intermediate understanding of information technology environments, customer onboarding workflows, and basic cybersecurity or compliance concepts. Prior experience in IAM, fraud operations, digital banking operations, or privacy governance is helpful. No programming is required, but familiarity with web authentication flows, identity proofing steps, and control documentation will make the exercises easier to apply. The course is designed at an intermediate level, with advanced topics such as decentralized identity and verifiable credentials covered at an operational awareness level rather than full implementation depth.
